comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4, C19-C22 regarding FAK expression patterns in human and mouse tissues. Both evaluations find the IHC staining data solid and well-supported, with reviewers specifically praising the strength of expression data across species.

Perfect agreement on claims C5, C27-C36 regarding tumor incidence and characteristics. Both evaluations strongly support the finding that FAK loss promotes BRAFV600E-induced tumorigenesis in the cecum, with reviewers noting the model closely resembles human sessile serrated adenoma/polyps.

Both support claims C37-C41, C43, C45 regarding molecular characterization and similarity to human SSA/Ps. However, peer reviewers note a limitation that OpenEval also identified: the murine data is largely confined to the cecum, and both acknowledge the small exome sequencing sample size (n=2).

Disagreement on claims C46, C48-C56 regarding cellular senescence and proliferation. OpenEval finds the negative results well-supported across multiple assays, while peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these claims in their grouped assessment.

Partial overlap on claims C49-C51 regarding inflammation. OpenEval finds inflammation is well-excluded by the data, but Reviewer 3 raises an alternative hypothesis that inflammation in the proximal colon could drive tumorigenesis, suggesting this mechanism remains incompletely ruled out.

Disagreement on claims C57, C59-C63 regarding pathway exclusions. OpenEval finds GSEA data appropriately rules out these pathways, but peer reviewers question reliance on GSEA alone, noting that lack of enrichment does not necessarily indicate pathways are uninvolved and requesting additional experiments on ERK target genes.

Disagreement on claims C64-C69, C72-C73 regarding differentiation and stemness. OpenEval supports the decoupling of differentiation and stemness, but peer reviewers question the functional role of Lgr4 and the stemness interpretation, with Reviewer 3 stating uncertainty about hypothesizing a stem cell role for LGR4.

Disagreement on claims C74-C82 regarding fetal stem cell program and Lgr4. OpenEval finds the evidence strong with appropriate citations, though notes the causal link is correlative. Peer reviewers are more critical, questioning whether Lgr4 upregulation is cecum-specific and requesting verification of the fetal stem cell signature using methods beyond GSEA.

Disagreement on claims C85-C94 regarding ERK phosphorylation and transcriptional decoupling. OpenEval finds the immunoblotting data well-supported with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers express concern that conclusions rely heavily on bioinformatic analyses and request additional experiments to examine ERK target gene expression directly.

Partial overlap on claims C90-C93 regarding FAK/EGFR interaction context. OpenEval supports the specificity to BRAFV600E context, while peer reviewers find it interesting but note the mechanism is incompletely understood and request additional studies on how FAK loss specifically decreases EGFR/ERK signaling in BRAFV600E context.

Partial agreement on claims C95-C103 regarding FAK kinase activity independence. OpenEval finds the co-IP data supportive though notes C103 is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers note the mechanism is incompletely understood and request additional mechanistic studies.

Disagreement on claims C106-C112 regarding ERK phosphorylation and Lgr4 regulation. OpenEval finds the qRT-PCR and cycloheximide chase data supportive despite acknowledging lack of statistical significance in some comparisons. Peer reviewers raise significant concerns about the protein stability data, noting discrepancies in Lgr4 half-life compared to prior publications and that experiments were only performed in one cell line rather than murine cecal organoids.

Disagreement on claims C113-C119 regarding NEDD4-mediated Lgr4 ubiquitination. OpenEval finds the mechanism well-demonstrated by immunoblotting and ubiquitination assays. Peer reviewers identify significant weaknesses: NEDD4 levels analyzed in only one mouse per group, mechanisms by which FAK loss regulates NEDD4 are unclear, and the relative contribution of altered mRNA expression versus ubiquitination has not been investigated.

Agreement on claims C120-C129 regarding KRAS context specificity. OpenEval supports the KC/FKC experiments as important negative controls demonstrating context-dependence. Peer reviewers view this as strong supporting evidence for specificity, with Reviewer 1 noting it provides strong evidence for the model, though additional mechanistic studies are requested.

Agreement on claims C132-C133, C135-C136, C139 regarding TCGA analysis and human relevance. Both evaluations support the human data analysis, with OpenEval noting limited sample sizes for some comparisons and peer reviewers accepting the correlation with patient samples and TCGA database as creating a solid basis for the model.

Partial agreement on claims C140-C146, C157-C158 regarding the integrative model. OpenEval finds the model well-supported though somewhat inferential. Peer reviewers acknowledge the novelty but question completeness, with the editor noting the mechanism is incomplete and Reviewer 3 stating the functional mechanism is quite correlative.

Partial agreement on claims C151-C152 regarding novelty and mechanistic conclusions. OpenEval finds the novelty claim justified and mechanistic conclusion well-supported. Peer reviewers acknowledge novelty but note the evidence is generally solid while the mechanistic data are incomplete.

OpenEval evaluates claims C104-C105 regarding organoid context-dependence as uncertain, noting C105 is speculative without validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims.

OpenEval supports claims C130-C131 regarding clinical knowledge about anti-EGFR therapy in KRAS-mutant CRC based on established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C155-C156, C159-C160 regarding therapeutic implications as uncertain, noting they are speculative proposals lacking direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these future therapeutic speculations.

OpenEval supports claims C161-C162 regarding tumor location similarity to human disease based on established clinical knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims.
OpenEval supports claims C1-C3, C8-C18 as background claims with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background context claims.
OpenEval supports claims C23-C26 as background claims establishing the unexpected nature of findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval supports numerous background claims (C42, C44, C47, C64, C70-C71, C74-C76, C83, C86, C89, C100, C113, C121-C122, C128, C134, C137-C138, C147-C150, C153-C154) with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these individual background claims.

Peer reviewers express concerns about mechanistic evidence for claim C6 and related claims (C58, C85, C87, C88), noting conclusions rely heavily on bioinformatic analyses and lack of enrichment does not prove pathways are uninvolved. OpenEval addresses these claims separately across multiple results (R5, R8) with different evaluations.
